newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends flat in lackluster trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends flat in lackluster trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar closed almost unchanged on Tuesday at C$1.3848 (US$0.7221) from this morning's open of C$1.3847 (US$0.7222). * Dealers said volumes were very light and contributed to narrow range trading for much of the session. * Currency appeared to stablilize after moving lower as traders tried to prompt a Bank of Canada rate hike.

Dealers said the currency stabilized after several sessions of weakness, which was seen by some in financial markets as an attempt to pressure the Bank of Canada to hike rates for a second time this year.

"There could still be some (Canadian) exporters looking to dump a lot of currency if we get around C$1.39. I think some exporters still have a few more (U.S.) dollars to go and so that could put a bit of a bottom on Canada if it does start to weaken off," the dealer said.
Analysts said the focus for many in the market remained U.S. payrolls data for July due out on Friday.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar slid to 1.3263 marks from Monday's close of 1.3293 marks but rose to 85.47 yen from Monday's 85 yen close.
